title: Minimum Time to Reach Destination in Directed Graph
summary: Given an integer n and a directed graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where each edge has a time range, find the minimum time to reach node n-1 from node 0.
statement: Given an integer n and a directed graph with n nodes labeled from 0 to n-1, where each edge has a time range, find the minimum time to reach node n-1 from node 0. If it's impossible, return -1. You can either wait at a node or travel along an edge if the current time falls within the edge's specified range.
constraints: Up to 100,000 nodes and directed timed edges.
An edge may be entered at any integer time in its inclusive availability interval.
Waiting and traversing each take one time unit; return -1 when unreachable.
hints: Only the earliest arrival at a node can improve future departures.
Run Dijkstra with waiting folded into each edge relaxation.
Depart at max(arrival,start) when it is no later than end, then arrive one unit later.
Waiting preserves FIFO order, so later arrivals cannot dominate earlier ones.
